_note: Drafted 2026-10-02 by a fresh AI agent from the PDF and the database concepts (after the user's manual chunk deletions), deciding edges by meaning, not PDF order. To be reviewed by the user.

reasons.environment -> people_depend: Saying people get air, water, food and shelter 'from the environment' needs the learner to know what an environment is.
reasons.basic_needs -> people_depend: The section walks through air, water, food and shelter one by one, so the learner must first know these are the basic needs.
reasons.environment -> animals_depend: The carabao, bird, fish and frog examples show animals using mud, trees, ponds and water, which assumes the learner knows these make up an environment.
reasons.basic_needs -> animals_depend: Each animal example shows a basic need (food, shelter, air) being met, so the learner must know the basic needs first.
reasons.environment -> plants_depend: Plants taking sunlight, water, air and soil from their surroundings only makes sense once the learner knows what an environment holds.
reasons.basic_needs -> plants_depend: The section explains how plants meet their needs, including sunlight to make food, which is introduced with the basic needs.
reasons.animals_depend -> aquarium_model: The aquarium asks what the fish and snail get from the tank, which applies how animals get food, air and shelter from their surroundings.
reasons.plants_depend -> aquarium_model: The aquarium asks what the kangkong gets from the tank, which applies how plants use water, light and air to make food.
reasons.animals_depend -> depend_on_each_other: The idea that animals eat plants or other animals and use plants for shelter builds on how animals get food and shelter.
reasons.plants_depend -> depend_on_each_other: The food chain starts with a rice plant using sunlight to make its food, which the learner must already know plants do.
reasons.people_depend -> environment_changes: To see that dirty rivers and smoky air hurt people (lost fish, hard to breathe), the learner must know people get food and air from the environment.
reasons.animals_depend -> environment_changes: To see that cutting trees takes away birds' homes, the learner must know animals get shelter from the environment.
reasons.plants_depend -> environment_changes: To see that garbage kills water plants and rain washes away soil, the learner must know plants need clean water and soil.

notes: 1062 'What I Need to Know' is the objectives list; unscored (null).
1067 and 1069 have the same title 'The Basic Needs of Living Things': a split pair (definition text and Figure 1 description), so both carry the key basic_needs.
1069's second chunk is machine alt text that is partly wrong: it says the plants box includes 'soil with nutrients', which actually comes from the table below the figure, not the figure.

1071 'Shelter' is the fourth bullet (houses of wood, bamboo, nipa) of the 'How People Depend on the Environment' list in 1070; extraction split it off and turned the bullet label into a title. It is given the same key people_depend. If the user would rather score it on its own, it would depend on environment and basic_needs and be parallel to people_depend.

environment and basic_needs are marked parallel: a basic need is defined without the idea of an environment, and an environment is defined without basic needs. This is a judgement call; a teacher could reasonably teach either first.

aquarium_model and depend_on_each_other are neither required nor parallel: the aquarium mentions plants giving fish a hiding place and plant bits as snail food, a weak link to living things depending on each other that could be argued in either direction.
depend_on_each_other -> environment_changes was considered (fish die, so people lose food) but not required; a Grade 3 learner can understand pollution harming living things without the food chain.
